ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Two small balls A and B of mass M with holes in their centers are connected by a light spring and sleeved on a horizontal smooth crossbar. A light spring is connected below each of the two small balls. The lower ends of the two light springs are tied to the same small ball C of mass m, as shown in Figure 7. It is known that the stiffness coefficients of the three light springs are all k, and the three light springs just form an equilateral triangle. Then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The elongation of the light spring connected to the small ball of mass m is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3k}mg$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Two small balls A and B of mass M with holes in their centers are connected by a light spring and sleeved on a horizontal smooth crossbar. A light spring is connected below each of the two small balls respectively; the lower ends of the two light springs are tied to the same small ball C of mass m, as shown in Figure 7. It is known that the stiffness coefficients of the three light springs are all k, and the three light springs just form an equilateral triangle. Find the elongation of the light spring connected to the small ball C of mass m.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The elongation of the light spring connected to the small ball of mass m is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3k}mg$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a horizontal crossbar; the left and right two red small balls A and B are sleeved on the crossbar, and A and B are connected by a horizontal light spring; from A and B respectively, one inclined light spring is connected downward from each, and the lower ends of the two inclined springs are jointly connected to the green small ball C below. The three springs form an equilateral triangle, so the two inclined springs connected to C both make a 60° angle with the direction of the horizontal rod, and are left-right symmetric. Then reason: Small ball C is subjected to gravity mg downward and to the pulling forces of the left and right two identical inclined springs. Because the configuration is left-right symmetric, the magnitudes of the pulling forces of the two inclined springs are equal; let the pulling force of each be F, and their horizontal components cancel each other. When in equilibrium in the vertical direction, the sum of the vertical components of the pulling forces of the two springs equals the gravity: 2F sin60° = mg. Since sin60° = sqrt(3)/2, sqrt(3)F = mg, giving F = mg/sqrt(3). By Hooke's law F = kx, the elongation of each light spring connected to C is x = F/k = mg/(sqrt(3)k) = sqrt(3)mg/(3k).
